presets.name: Bare
presets.description: The style stripped back: no background, so the avatar sits on whatever your page is, and the facial hair component switched off.

presets.name: Sepia
presets.summary: One warm brown for skin, hair and shirt.
presets.description: A real sepia print, which means the skin tone goes with it. Every other preset here leaves skin to the seed; this one cannot, because a color photograph of a face is not sepia. Six hairstyles carry a colored cap or band and two mouths a pink that no option reaches, so those drop out.

presets.name: Greyscale
presets.description: Properly grey rather than grey hair on a colored face. Useful for a print stylesheet, a disabled state, or anywhere color would carry meaning it should not. Six hairstyles carry a colored cap or band and two mouths a pink that no option reaches, so those drop out.

presets.name: Duotone
presets.summary: Three steps of one indigo and nothing else.
presets.description: Background, skin, hair and clothing take the same hue at different lightnesses. As with Sepia, a duotone only works if the face joins in, so the seed loses its say over skin here. Six hairstyles carry a colored cap or band and two mouths a pink that no option reaches, so those drop out.

presets.name: Muted
presets.summary: Dusty clothing and hair, nothing shouts.
presets.description: The style ships seven saturated clothing colors and a hair palette that runs to pink. This replaces both with dusty tones, for interfaces where the avatar should be present without being the loudest thing on screen.

presets.name: Electric
presets.summary: Clothing at full saturation on near black.
presets.description: The other direction on the same lever. Only the clothing changes: six colors at the top of their saturation. Hair stays natural on purpose, because two loud layers cancel each other out and the shirt is the larger area.

presets.name: Pastel Wall
presets.summary: Five soft backgrounds, everything else untouched.
presets.description: Changes nothing about the people, only what they stand in front of. The lightest way to make a set of avatars feel like it belongs together.

presets.name: Bold Pop
presets.description: The loud counterpart to Pastel Wall. Strong enough that the avatar holds its own against a busy page, and the only preset here that will fight with a colorful interface rather than sit inside it.

presets.name: Sunrise
presets.summary: A warm gradient behind, everything else untouched.
presets.description: Shows the gradient background options: two colors, a linear fill and a fixed angle. The seed still decides which of the two ends up on top.

presets.name: Night Shift
presets.summary: Near black behind, light clothing in front.
presets.description: For dark interfaces. The clothing pool drops to the light end so the figure does not disappear into the background.

presets.name: Full Cast
presets.description: The facial hair component sits at ten percent, so a small set shows it on nobody. This raises it, which is what you want when showing the style off rather than filling a user list.

presets.name: Close Up
presets.summary: Scaled in on the face, for small avatars.
presets.description: Uses scale rather than color. At the size a comment thread gives an avatar, the default framing spends a lot of it on empty space, and cropping in buys the detail back.
